memories.content: Conduct one review prior to submission focusing solely on the validity of user problems, design interventions, and evaluation logic.
Cross-check whether research questions align with the core functions of the prototype.
Cross-check whether evaluation tasks align with representative measures.
Cross-check whether collected evidence aligns with design and operational decisions to be changed.
Verify at the end that user problems, design interventions, user studies, and expected contributions form a coherent logical flow.
HCI reviewers view the validity of design interventions as low if research questions are not linked to prototype functions.
HCI reviewers view the validity of evaluation plans as low if evaluation tasks do not produce representative measures.
HCI reviewers view the practicality of contributions as low if collected evidence cannot change design or operational decisions.
Cross-check at the end whether each research question, formative evaluation data, and design modification judgment are seamlessly connected.
Review whether the application conditions of proposed design principles and boundary cases of failure are presented together.
The user can have contributions reviewed only if prototype outcomes and the transferable design knowledge derived from them are separated.
The scope of observation in controlled formative evaluations does not include long-term adaptation and operational changes in real-world usage contexts.
Use an em dash only for a deliberate interruption or sharp contrast; otherwise split the sentence or choose ordinary punctuation.
In procedural passages, begin each sentence with the action, condition, or output instead of repeating “we” so the steps remain easy to follow and reuse.
Write system behaviors confirmed in the actual usage environment as observed states.
Write system behaviors not yet confirmed in the field as conditional plans.
Readers can reconstruct a sequence more accurately when each sentence begins with the action or condition rather than the author.
Do not mechanically split connected thoughts into separate short sentences when doing so destroys the intended reading rhythm.
Preserve a longer sentence when its clauses form one continuous movement that is easier to follow together than apart.
The user understands that short sentences are easier to scan but feels that uniformly segmented prose loses its reading rhythm.
Write procedural sentences so their opening phrase can be reused as a checklist item without changing the step's meaning.
The user should choose “I” as an individual author or “we” for a named team and should not mix them when describing the same responsible party.
Action-first procedural sentences can be reordered or copied into a checklist more easily because their subject is the step rather than the proposal author.
The user can explain whether an em dash marks an intentional interruption or contrast rather than using it decoratively.
An em dash creates a stronger interruption than a comma and can make a deliberate contrast easier to hear in the sentence.

analysis.overview: The frames address separate concerns: the reference frame governs HCI proposal validity and evidentiary coherence, while the compared frame governs prose structure, punctuation, authorial voice, and calibration of claims to field evidence. Neither supplies a scope-aligned counterpart to the other.

relations.reason: This establishes a one-sided review scope with no corresponding writing-policy claim in the compared frame.
relations.summary: A pre-submission review should focus exclusively on the validity of user problems, design interventions, and evaluation logic.

relations.reason: The memories state the same one-sided alignment check and its reviewer-facing rationale.
relations.summary: Research questions should be linked to prototype functions to support the validity of design interventions.

relations.reason: The memories state the same one-sided evaluation alignment requirement and its rationale.
relations.summary: Evaluation tasks should yield representative measures to support the validity of the evaluation plan.

relations.reason: The memories express the same one-sided requirement linking evidence to consequential decisions.
relations.summary: Collected evidence should be capable of changing design or operational decisions so contributions remain practical.

relations.reason: Both memories specify complementary checks of the same one-sided end-to-end logical flow.
relations.summary: The proposal should present a coherent chain connecting problems or questions, evaluation evidence, design judgments, and contributions.

relations.reason: This is an independent one-sided requirement for bounding design knowledge.
relations.summary: Proposed design principles should present their application conditions alongside failure boundary cases.

relations.reason: This is an independent one-sided condition for reviewable contribution framing.
relations.summary: Prototype outcomes should be separated from the transferable design knowledge derived from them when presenting contributions.

relations.reason: This is an independent one-sided limitation on the evidentiary scope of formative evaluation.
relations.summary: Controlled formative evaluations do not observe long-term adaptation or operational change in real-world use.

relations.reason: The memories jointly state the same one-sided punctuation policy, its perceptual effect, and the author's ability to justify its use.
relations.summary: An em dash should mark a deliberate strong interruption or sharp contrast rather than serve as decorative punctuation.

relations.reason: The memories restate one one-sided action-first writing policy and its navigation and reuse benefits.
relations.summary: Procedural sentences should begin with the action, condition, or output so steps are clear, reorderable, and reusable as checklist items.

relations.reason: The memories express the same one-sided preference and its tradeoff between scanability and rhythm.
relations.summary: Connected thoughts should remain in a longer sentence when mechanical segmentation would damage an otherwise clear reading rhythm.

relations.reason: The memories split one one-sided writing policy according to explicit evidence-status conditions.
relations.summary: System behavior should be described as observed when field-confirmed and as conditional when not yet field-confirmed.

relations.reason: This is an independent one-sided policy for consistent authorial responsibility.
relations.summary: Use “I” for an individual author or “we” for a named team without mixing them for the same responsible party.

reports.compared_only: The compared frame covers action-first reusable procedures, evidence-calibrated descriptions of behavior, sentence rhythm, deliberate em-dash use, and consistent authorial pronouns.
reports.reference_only: The reference frame covers pre-submission validity checks, coherent links among research, design, evaluation, and decisions, contribution framing, design-principle boundaries, and limits of controlled formative evidence.
